title: Power Pages: create a single-page application (SPA) site from Power Pages studio
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing qualifications and documented governance controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes the planned studio entry point from the existing CLI workflow and leaves the studio option's default and specific requirements open.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let makers create a modern SPA site directly from Power Pages studio.
claims.quote: Quickly get started with modern single-page application (SPA) development by creating a site directly from Power Pages Studio.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes continuing development and customisation using preferred development tools and frameworks.
claims.quote: Continue building and customizing your experience using your preferred development tools and frameworks.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; summary; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the planned studio SPA creation flow as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages studio create SPA single page application site prerequisites enable default setting; opened /power-pages/configure/create-code-sites and /power-pages/getting-started/create-manage. Results describe CLI uploads and traditional studio templates, not the planned studio SPA flow.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk

None states the studio option's default or a change to existing sites.

claims.claim: Learn defines an SPA site as a Power Pages site running entirely in the user's browser with client-side rendering.
claims.quote: An SPA site is a Power Pages site that runs entirely in the user's browser (client-side rendering).

claims.claim: The SPA documentation describes creating and setting up a project using the Power Platform CLI.
claims.quote: Create and set up an SPA project for Power Pages by using the Power Platform CLI (PAC CLI).

claims.claim: pac pages upload-code-site uploads SPA site assets.
claims.quote: Use the pac pages upload-code-site command to upload your local source and compiled assets to your Power Pages environment.

claims.claim: A newly uploaded SPA site appears in Power Pages under Inactive sites.
claims.quote: After you upload a site, it appears in Power Pages in the Inactive sites list.

claims.claim: The uploaded site must be activated to make it available to users.
claims.quote: Activate the site to make it available to users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The pages workspace is not supported for the documented SPA sites.
claims.quote: The pages workspace isn't supported. Use client routing and client site pages.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Liquid code and Liquid templates are not supported for the documented SPA sites.
claims.quote: Liquid code and Liquid templates aren't supported. Access data by using your framework's template engine and Web APIs.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding out-of-the-box components such as lists and forms is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Adding out-of-the-box components like lists and forms isn't currently supported. However, you can build custom forms and lists by using the React framework and Web APIs.

claims.claim: Learn says SPA sites are managed only through source code and CLI tools.
claims.quote: Unlike traditional Power Pages sites, you manage SPA sites only through source code and command-line interface (CLI) tools.

claims.claim: How the roadmap's studio entry point fits with Learn's source-code-and-CLI description is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages create single page application studio SPA site default enable disable licensing; Power Pages studio create SPA single page application site prerequisites enable default setting. Opened /power-pages/configure/create-code-sites and /power-pages/getting-started/create-manage.

claims.claim: The Power Pages plugin supports creating SPA sites from curated templates in GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code.
claims.quote: Create a site from a curated SPA template or scaffold it from scratch, then customize it, set up Dataverse data models, and configure authentication. Template creation is available in both GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code through /create-site.

claims.claim: SPA sites use the same security model as traditional Power Pages sites.
claims.quote: Power Pages SPA sites use the same security model as traditional Power Pages sites.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SPA code can read and modify Dataverse records through Power Pages Web APIs.
claims.quote: Developers can use Power Pages Web APIs to load content into the UI or to create, update, and delete records.

claims.claim: Required Web APIs must be enabled before use.
claims.quote: Before using these APIs, make sure that the required Web APIs are enabled and that appropriate table permissions and web roles are properly configured.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Table permissions govern data access through SPA Web API calls.
claims.quote: Power Pages enforces table permissions and security web roles on Web API calls, ensuring that data access aligns with user roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Web roles govern the site's Web API data access.
claims.quote: Power Pages enforces table permissions and security web roles on Web API calls, ensuring that data access aligns with user roles.

claims.claim: Creating a site in the default environment risks unintentionally sharing data with other users.
claims.quote: This environment is shared across all the users in the tenant and creating your site here risks sharing data with other users unintentionally.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not recommend creating a site in the default environment.
claims.quote: It isn't recommended to create a site in the default environment.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented SPA setup requires allowing JavaScript file uploads in Dataverse environments.
claims.quote: Allow JavaScript file uploads in Dataverse environments.

claims.claim: The blocked file extensions setting prevents uploading or downloading attachment types considered dangerous.
claims.quote: Block these file extensions | Prevent upload or download of certain attachment types that are considered dangerous.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing blocked extensions has environment-wide upload implications rather than affecting only Power Pages or SPA sites.
claims.quote: You can specify which types of files can't be saved in file columns, attachments and notes. ... It's stored in the Organization.BlockedAttachments column. There's only one row in the organization table.

claims.claim: Each new site automatically has a default Microsoft Entra ID provider.
claims.quote: Each new site automatically has a default Microsoft Entra ID provider.

claims.claim: Learn's local-development steps enable bearer authentication through site settings.
claims.quote:
Authentication/BearerAuthentication/Enabled = true
Authentication/BearerAuthentication/Protocol = OpenIdConnect
Authentication/BearerAuthentication/Provider = AzureAD

claims.claim: Learn's local-development steps set site visibility to Public.
claims.quote:
Set site visibility to Public

This setting lets localhost access the site for development and testing purposes.

claims.claim: Microsoft limits those local-development settings to development environments.
claims.quote: Apply these settings only in development environments.

claims.claim: The plugin documentation warns that AI-generated code and configuration can be inaccurate.
claims.quote: Code and configuration generated by the AI coding agent can be inaccurate.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing generated content before deployment.
claims.quote: Review, test, and validate all generated content before you approve or deploy it. Always review agent proposals before approving them.

claims.claim: The SPA page describes SEO support as limited.
claims.quote: Because SPA sites are built with the React framework and use client-side rendering, SEO support is limited.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages licensing is capacity based.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: One capacity type is Authenticated users per website/month.
claims.quote: offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The other capacity type is Anonymous users per website/month.
claims.quote: offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.claim: Authenticated user capacity is available as a subscription licence.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user capacity subscription license can be purchased for the anticipated number of unique, authenticated users.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: An authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter is available.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of authenticated users who have accessed a website in a month.

claims.claim: Anonymous user capacity is available as a subscription licence.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user monthly capacity subscription license can be purchased for the anticipated number of unique, anonymous users accessing a website in a month.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: An anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter is available.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of anonymous users who have accessed a website in a month.

claims.claim: The authenticated meter measures unique authenticated users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter: A measure of the number of unique authenticated users per website per month.

claims.claim: An administrator must allocate capacity to a Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: This capacity must be allocated to a Microsoft Power Platform environment by an administrator.

claims.claim: Administrators can download Power Pages authenticated and anonymous reports from the admin center capacity page.
claims.quote: Select Capacity. ... In the Add-ons section, select Download reports. ... Select the Power Pages authenticated or Power Pages anonymous report.

claims.claim: Authenticated users licensed with Power Apps or Dynamics 365 enterprise licences have Power Pages use rights.
claims.quote: Authenticated users licensed with Power Apps or Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses are granted use rights for Power Pages as described below.

claims.claim: Power Apps per app users can access one website in the environment assigned the per app capacity licences.
claims.quote: Power Apps per app: Users can access one Power Pages website that should be part of the environment to which Power Apps per app capacity licenses are assigned.

claims.claim: Power Apps per user licences give rights to unlimited Power Pages websites.
claims.quote: Power Apps per user licensed users: Users who have been assigned Power Apps per user licenses can use unlimited Power Pages websites.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 enterprise users have unlimited websites mapped to the licensed application context and its environment.
claims.quote: Users who have been assigned Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses can use unlimited Power Pages websites. These websites must map to the licensed Dynamics 365 application context and map to the same environment as the licensed Dynamics 365 application.

claims.claim: Recognising Power Apps per-user/premium and Dynamics 365 enterprise licences requires Entra ID access through the out-of-the-box Azure AD provider.
claims.quote: In order for Power Apps per users/premium and Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses to be recognized: ... Users should access the Power Pages site using their Entra ID and utilizing the out of the box Azure AD provider.

claims.claim: Those licences must be assigned in the same tenant as the Power Pages site to be recognised.
claims.quote: Users need a license assigned in the same tenant as the Power Pages site. If the user's license is assigned in a different tenant, it's not recognized.

claims.claim: The SPA page's prerequisite list names no licence.
claims.quote: A Power Pages environment with admin privileges. ... Power Platform CLI (PAC CLI) version 1.44.x or later installed and authenticated. ... A Power Pages site on version 9.7.4.x or later. ... Allow JavaScript file uploads ... A local Git repository

claims.claim: The CLI route requires Power Platform CLI version 1.44.x or later.

claims.claim: An admin center UI path for disabling non-administrator Power Pages site creation is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers admin center UI tenant site creation setting. Opened /power-pages/admin/control-site-creation; read search excerpts of /power-pages/admin/admin-overview. The tenant restriction is documented through PowerShell, not a UI path.

claims.claim: Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody @{ "disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers" = $true } disables tenant site creation by non-administrators.
claims.quote: Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody @{ "disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers" = $true }

claims.claim: Setting disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers to $false allows site creation again.
claims.quote: To enable site creation in a tenant, change the settings value from $true to $false.

claims.claim: For this tenant setting, administrators are users with Dynamics 365 administrator or Power Platform administrator Azure roles.
claims.quote: Administrators are the users having one of the following Azure roles: ... Dynamics 365 administrator ... Power Platform administrator ... Users without these Azure roles are considered non-administrators.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy + Security > Blocked Attachments.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... Select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Privacy + Security. ... In the Blocked Attachments section, remove js from the list of file extensions.

claims.claim: PATCH /organizations(organizationid), with blockedattachments in the request body, changes blocked file extensions.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /organizations(organizationid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... BlockedAttachments ... LogicalName | blockedattachments ... Prevent upload or download of certain attachment types that are considered dangerous.
